mcqs.question: Which of the following sequences correctly represents the general reactivity series of metals from most reactive to least reactive as given in NCERT Class 10?

options.A: Potassium, Sodium, Calcium, Magnesium, Aluminum, Zinc, Iron, Tin, Lead, Hydrogen, Copper, Silver, Gold, Platinum
options.B: Sodium, Potassium, Calcium, Magnesium, Zinc, Aluminum, Iron, Lead, Tin, Hydrogen, Copper, Silver, Gold, Platinum
options.C: Potassium, Calcium, Sodium, Magnesium, Aluminum, Iron, Zinc, Tin, Lead, Hydrogen, Copper, Silver, Gold, Platinum
options.D: Potassium, Sodium, Calcium, Magnesium, Zinc, Aluminum, Iron, Tin, Lead, Hydrogen, Copper, Silver, Gold, Platinum

mcqs.answer: Potassium, Sodium, Calcium, Magnesium, Aluminum, Zinc, Iron, Tin, Lead, Hydrogen, Copper, Silver, Gold, Platinum
mcqs.explanation: Option A lists the metals exactly in the order given in the NCERT general reactivity series (most to least reactive). The other options misplace metals, e.g., swapping Na and K or placing Zn before Al, which contradicts the standard series.

mcqs.question: When a strip of zinc metal is immersed in copper(II) sulfate solution, which of the following correctly describes the observed reaction?

options.A: Zinc metal dissolves, copper metal precipitates, forming zinc sulfate solution.
options.B: No visible change; both metals remain unchanged.
options.C: Copper metal dissolves, zinc metal precipitates, forming copper sulfate solution.
options.D: Both metals form a protective oxide layer preventing any reaction.

mcqs.answer: Zinc metal dissolves, copper metal precipitates, forming zinc sulfate solution.
mcqs.explanation: Zinc is higher than copper in the reactivity series, so it displaces copper from copper sulfate, producing ZnSO₄ in solution and solid Cu. Options B, C and D describe either no reaction or the opposite displacement, which are incorrect.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand reactions of metals with salt solutions
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes the reaction of iron with copper(II) sulfate solution from that of copper metal with iron(II) sulfate solution?

options.A: Iron displaces copper from its solution, while copper does not displace iron from its solution.
options.B: Both iron and copper displace each other from each other's solutions.
options.C: Neither iron nor copper displaces the other; both remain unchanged.
options.D: Copper displaces iron, while iron does not displace copper.

mcqs.answer: Iron displaces copper from its solution, while copper does not displace iron from its solution.
mcqs.explanation: Iron is above copper in the reactivity series, so Fe can displace Cu²⁺ ions, but Cu, being less reactive, cannot displace Fe²⁺ ions. Hence option A is correct; the other options contradict the series.

mcqs.question: Based on the reactivity series, which metal is more reactive?
mcqs.explanation: Magnesium appears above zinc, iron and copper in the reactivity series, indicating it is more reactive than all three. Therefore option A is correct; the others are less reactive.

mcqs.question: Which of the following metals can displace lead from a solution of lead nitrate?
mcqs.explanation: Zinc is placed above lead in the general reactivity series, so it can displace lead ions from lead nitrate. Copper, silver and gold are below lead and cannot displace it, making options B, C, D incorrect.

mcqs.question: A piece of aluminium foil is added to a solution of silver nitrate. What is the most likely outcome?

options.A: Aluminium displaces silver, forming aluminium nitrate and depositing silver metal.
options.B: No reaction occurs because aluminium is less reactive than silver.
options.C: Silver displaces aluminium, forming silver nitrate and depositing aluminium metal.
options.D: Both metals form a complex ion and remain in solution.

mcqs.answer: Aluminium displaces silver, forming aluminium nitrate and depositing silver metal.
mcqs.explanation: Aluminium is higher than silver in the reactivity series, so it can displace Ag⁺ ions, producing Al(NO₃)₃ and solid silver. Options B and C reverse the reactivity order, and D is not applicable.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand reactions of metals with salt solutions
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements reflects a common misconception about metal‑salt reactions?

options.A: All metals will react with any salt solution to give a displacement reaction.
options.B: Only metals placed above a given metal in the reactivity series can displace it from its salt solution.
options.C: Metals below hydrogen in the series do not react with dilute acids.
options.D: A metal can displace a less reactive metal from its compound solution.

mcqs.answer: All metals will react with any salt solution to give a displacement reaction.
mcqs.explanation: The statement in option A is false; only metals higher than the other in the reactivity series can cause displacement. Options B, C and D correctly describe the reactivity series principles, so they are not misconceptions.

mcqs.question: Metal X displaces metal Y from its salt solution, but metal Y does not displace metal Z from its salt solution. Which of the following correctly orders the metals from most to least reactive?
mcqs.explanation: If X can displace Y, X is more reactive than Y. If Y cannot displace Z, Y is less reactive than Z, so the order is X > Y > Z. Option A reflects this; the other options violate the given displacement observations.
